sigma[2,1]<-sigma[1,2]<-1

#simulating data
 mydata<-simdata(a,d,3000,itemtype,mu=mu,sigma=sigma)

 When I calibrate item scores with using mod1<-mirt(mydata,1), estimated parameters are close to my target paramaters. But when I use PARSCALE for calibrating, I received different item paramaters. For example for item 1 a=0.555 d=0.623
 My question is why mirt package and PARSCALE produce different results?

messages.author: 70d0917afd869432
messages.subject: Re: about calibratiıng data
parts:
Hi Neese,

mirt uses a different parameterization for a and d than the traditional IRT metric that PARSCALE uses.  If you've done everything correctly, the a parameter should match across results from mirt and PARSCALE; but the d will differ.  You can convert the parameters easily by hand by using:

b = - d / a

Further,

z = a(Theta - b) = a Theta + d

So,

d = - a*b

The developer has also included an option in the latest version of the package to do this automatically for you via coef() 

Cheers,

Matt
